provenance.note: Generated by drivers/regression on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==4.2.3. Two library changes since 3.20.0 reshaped the performance/stability story: 4.2.2 rewrote the CPU least-squares core (qr_solve) to a single-pass rank-revealing QR matching R's lm.fit/glm.fit, so CPU OLS/GLM now MEET OR BEAT R (speedup_vs_r > 1 across all families on both hosts -- at 3.20.0 the CPU was slower); and 4.2.3 replaced the float32 GPU IRLS round-off-floor stop with a Newton-decrement stop plus descent step-halving, so the plain (unpenalized) float32 GPU GLM -- including the log-link Poisson/Gamma families that FAILED LOUD at 3.20.0 -- now converges (~1e-6 vs CPU) on both MPS and CUDA. Correctness vs R is unchanged (round-off). Hosts: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32, R 4.5.2) and forge (NVIDIA CUDA, CPU fp64 + CUDA fp32/fp64, R 4.3.3).
provenance.baseline: Compare against reports/regression-v3.20.0.md. Correctness identical (round-off). The changes are speed (CPU now beats R, was slower) and GPU stability (plain float32 log-link now converges, was the 'plain fails / ridge holds' demonstration).

reference.name: R stats::lm / stats::glm / MASS::glm.nb
reference.what: R's lm() (OLS via pivoted QR) and glm() (GLM via IRLS), plus MASS::glm.nb() for the negative binomial. pystatistics unifies lm and glm, so the head-to-head pulls from both. Ridge is cross-checked against MASS::lm.ridge / glmnet in the drivers.

studies.title: Correctness vs R — Powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU / fp64)
studies.note: CPU OLS + 5 GLM families vs R on real datasets. Coefficients match R to round-off (~1e-11..1e-15; negbin coef ~1e-4 and gamma/poisson SEs ~1e-3..1e-8 are the documented dispersion/theta tolerances). As of 4.2.2 the CPU fit also MEETS/BEATS R on wall-clock (speedup_vs_r 1.4-2.8x here) -- the Prime-Directive parity requirement.

studies.title: Correctness vs R — Forge (Linux x86-64, CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Second-host CPU-vs-R correctness (Forge, R 4.3.3): identical round-off agreement; CPU speedup_vs_r 2.2-5x (CPU beats R).

studies.title: Device scaling — Powerhouse: CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32)
studies.note: OLS + GLM device scaling, CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32). The CPU baseline is faster than at 3.20.0 (4.2.2 Core-QR); the GPU is faster still where float32 is stable.

studies.title: Device scaling — Forge: CPU (fp64) vs CUDA (fp32)
studies.note: OLS + GLM device scaling, CPU (fp64) vs CUDA (fp32).

studies.title: GPU GLM stability at scale — Powerhouse (MPS): plain fails, ridge holds
studies.note: GPU GLM stability at scale (MPS). FLIPPED at 4.2.3: the plain (unpenalized) float32 log-link fit, which FAILED LOUD at 3.20.0, now CONVERGES (plain_status=converged, plain_rel_vs_cpu ~1e-7 vs CPU) thanks to the 4.2.3 Newton-decrement stop + descent step-halving. Ridge still holds; fp64 is unsupported on MPS (no float64).

studies.title: GPU GLM stability at scale — Forge (CUDA): plain, ridge, and fp64
studies.note: GPU GLM stability at scale (CUDA). Plain float32 log-link now CONVERGES (~1e-6 vs CPU, was fail-loud at 3.20.0); ridge converges; gpu_fp64 is exact (~1e-15). The 4.2.3 fp32 stop-rule fix resolved the plain-log-link failure on CUDA as well as MPS.

record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over the coefficient vector (correctness headline)
record_fields.se_max_rel: max relative difference over the standard-error vector
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.peak_mem_mb: peak memory during the fit (GPU allocator high-water mark; process RSS delta on CPU)
record_fields.plain_status: outcome of a plain GPU GLM fit at scale: converged or raised (fails loud when float32 is unreliable)
record_fields.ridge_status: outcome of a ridge GPU GLM fit (the penalty conditions the float32 solve)
record_fields.ridge_rel_vs_cpu_ridge: ||Δβ||/||β|| of the ridge GPU fit vs the CPU ridge fit (float32 tier)
record_fields.fp64_status: gpu_fp64 outcome — converged on CUDA, unsupported on MPS (no float64)
record_fields.fp64_rel_vs_cpu: ||Δβ||/||β|| of the gpu_fp64 fit vs the CPU fit (~1e-15, numerically exact)
